reading.text:
UNIT def:LevyStochCalc.Probability.aug
Standing setting (paper section 2, intro (eq:mvfbsdej), section 3 solution space, section 4,
appendix A): (Omega, F, (F_t), P) satisfying the usual conditions, horizon T > 0; a d-dim
Brownian motion W and an independent Poisson random measure N on R_+ x E with intensity
dt nu(de), nu sigma-finite on a countably generated (E, calE); (F_t) is the usual augmentation
of the filtration generated by W, N and an independent initial sigma-field F_0. The compensated
measure is Ntilde(dt,de) = N(dt,de) - dt nu(de). Integrands U of the Poisson integral are
predictable: P (x) calE-measurable, P the predictable sigma-field on Omega x [0,T]
(eq:fubiniiso), with E int_0^T ||U_t||^2_{L2(nu)} dt < infinity (the space H^2_N). The
integral int_0^t int_E U_s(e) Ntilde(ds,de) is the standard L2 (Ito-Levy) compensated-Poisson
integral: an L2 martingale, cadlag, with the isometry E|int_0^t int U dNtilde|^2 =
E int_0^t ||U_s||^2 ds (used in Lemma 4.1 "true L2-martingales by the Ito and
compensated-Poisson isometries"), jumps Delta = U_s(e) at atoms (s,e) of N, and for integrands
in L1(dP dt nu) the integral splits as int U dN - int U nu ds (eq:compid, eq:zeromean).
Progressive measurability is used for the coefficient processes b, sigma, f and the forcings
q^b, q^sigma, q^f (eq:coefmeas, section 4); predictability (P (x) calE) for h and q^h.

Reading.
Paper notion: "the usual augmentation" of the filtration generated by W, N and F_0, giving a
filtered space "satisfying the usual conditions" (complete and right-continuous). Standard
definition: F^aug_t = intersection over s > t of sigma(F_s, calN), calN the P-null sets (of the
P-completion of the ambient sigma-algebra). Faithful Lean: for each t, the sigma-algebra
generated by F_{t+} (or F_s for all s > t, intersected) together with the P-null sets. In Lean
the ambient sigma-algebra is fixed and a Filtration must be contained in it, so only null sets
measurable for the ambient sigma-algebra can be adjoined: a representation choice, harmless for
almost-sure statements (and exact if the ambient space is complete). Edge cases: at the last time
of a bounded time index the right limit is F_T itself; if the definition adjoins null sets only
(no right-continuous regularization), it is the "augmentation", not the "usual augmentation" -
equal for the Brownian-Poisson natural filtration (a theorem: the augmented Levy filtration is
right-continuous) but not as a definition; if it takes the right-continuous regularization only
(no null sets), it is not the usual augmentation either. The definition must be a filtration
(monotone, within the ambient sigma-algebra).

comparison.text:
Lean (LevyStochCalc/Probability/Augmentation.lean): aug m m0 mu : MeasurableSpace Omega, the
sets A that are m0-measurable and differ from some m-measurable B by a mu-null set
(mu (A symmDiff B) = 0); aug_eq_sup_nullSigma: aug m m0 mu = m sup (sigma of m0-measurable
mu-null sets) when m <= m0; aug_le: aug <= m0; le_aug: m <= aug.
Comparison with the locked reading: the reading took the paper notion "usual augmentation" of a
filtration (null sets and right-continuity). The Lean unit is a sigma-algebra-level operation:
the augmentation by null sets, i.e. the completion part of the usual augmentation; the
filtration-level object built from it is Brownian.augFiltration (seq t = aug (F (max t 0)) m0 mu)
and the joint Levy filtration, outside this unit. Item by item:
 - null sets adjoined: yes, but only the m0-measurable mu-null sets (a Lean Filtration must stay
   inside m0): a representation choice, harmless for almost-sure statements and exact when m0 is
   P-complete; the paper's "complete" basis is represented this way;
 - right-continuity: not part of aug. For the Brownian-Poisson filtration the null-set
   augmentation is right-continuous (the library proves rightCont_augFiltration_eq,
   "A_{t+} = A_t for t >= 0", Driver/AugJointRightCont.lean), so the null-set augmentation is the
   usual augmentation there, as the reading anticipated ("equal for the Brownian-Poisson natural
   filtration (a theorem) but not as a definition");
 - edge cases: aug m m0 mu needs no hypothesis m <= m0 (if m is not inside m0 the result is
   still inside m0 and contains the m0-measurable sets a.e. equal to m-sets) - harmless; it is a
   sigma-algebra (proved fields).
Verdict reasoning: faithful as the null-set augmentation of a sigma-algebra; the usual
augmentation of the paper is aug (applied timewise) plus a proved right-continuity, not aug alone.

verdict.detail:
Representation choices: (1) only m0-measurable mu-null sets are adjoined (a Lean Filtration must
stay inside the ambient sigma-algebra m0), harmless for almost-sure statements and exact when m0
is P-complete; (2) aug is the null-set augmentation of a sigma-algebra, not the right-continuous
regularisation: the paper's "usual augmentation" is aug applied timewise (Brownian.augFiltration)
plus right-continuity, which the library proves for the augmented Levy filtration
(rightCont_augFiltration_eq, Driver/AugJointRightCont.lean), so for the paper's filtration the
two coincide; (3) no hypothesis m <= m0 needed (the result is always inside m0).
